title: ReadMe Ships Restless Tool for AI Agents Generating 72% of Doc Traffic
summary:
Failed API responses will now include direct fix steps and documentation links via a new tool designed to assist autonomous software agents. Developed by the team behind ReadMe, Restless embeds resolution instructions into error messages so that AI agents can resolve failures without needing to search manually for technical guides. The system captures live traffic to convert agent feedback into tickets for Linear or suggested updates to documentation.

AI agents currently generate 72% of all traffic to API documentation, yet they rarely consult these resources when a request fails. Restless addresses this by allowing developers to initialize the system via a "npx restless init" command and supporting integration with Claude Code or Codex. Agents can additionally search and replay their own API calls through a hosted MCP server.

Agents are quickly becoming your API and docs' main users.

The @readme team says agents now make up 72% of traffic to API docs. And when an agent gets stuck, it rarely goes looking for the docs.

Restless puts the fix steps and a doc link right in the error response. If the agent is still stuck, it can report what is missing, and that turns into doc updates or issues.

I build a lot of agents that call APIs, and I want every API to have this.
